title: Permafrost carbon feedback quantification
bottleneck: Permafrost holds ~1,500 billion tonnes of carbon — twice the atmosphere's — and thaw could release 5-15 percent of it by 2100, yet the feedback's magnitude is deeply uncertain: bottom-up and top-down estimates disagree on whether the far north is currently a net source or sink, abrupt thaw (thermokarst) can double local emissions but is barely in models, and sunlight-driven photomineralization of thaw carbon in waterways adds ~14 percent that no model includes. Most IPCC-class models still omit or underplay the feedback.
why_it_blocks: An uncounted feedback means carbon budgets are overstated: one 2026 study estimated natural systems could amplify warming 20-30 percent beyond modeled projections. Every year the feedback stays unquantified, mitigation targets rest on a potentially false baseline.
current_state: The Permafrost Carbon Network is synthesizing abrupt-thaw literature, and new models couple permafrost modules to carbon-cycle ensembles. But the Arctic's remoteness keeps observations sparse, and uncertainty ranges remain as wide as the estimates themselves.
